newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castor futures market closed for festival.
newsitem.headline: Indian castor futures market closed for festival.

text.p: The Bombay Oilseeds and Oils Exchange, which conducts futures trading in castorseed, was closed on Wednesday for a Hindu festival.
On Tuesday castorseed June delivery dropped 13 rupees to 1,160/1,161 rupees per quintal on fresh speculative selling.
"Sluggish overseas buying and higher arrivals prompted fresh speculative selling," said a trader.
Arrivals of castorseed had picked up since last week at the end of a 10-day truck strike, he said.
The daily average arrivals of castorseed in India's western state of Gujarat, the country's main producer, rose considerably, the trader added.

In edible oils, groundnut oil was steady at 356/357 rupees per 10 kg in limited trade. Imported palm-oil was steady at 285 rupees per 10 kg. Sentiment was subdued as traders expected the arrival of about 15,000/20,000 tonnes of imported palm oil at Bombay's port in the current month.
In Rajkot, spot groundnut oil was steady at 540/545 rupees per 15 kg.
